rows.speaker: بحر العلوم
rows.claim: The manifest Book is the Preserved Tablet: it clarifies what is written there about all that will occur.
rows.anchor: وفي بحر العلوم الكتاب المبين هو اللوح وإبانته أنه قد كتب وبين فيه كل ما هو كائن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabic is a relational description of the Qur’an’s language after revelation; it was already Qur’an before being sent down.
rows.anchor: فعربيا نعت لقرآنا نعت نسبة ، لا نعت لزوم ، لأنه كان قرآنا قبل نزوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Qur’an” is a preparatory circumstantial noun whose following adjective supplies the actual state being described.
rows.anchor: وقرآنا حال موطئة ، أي توطئة للحال التي هي عربيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The purpose is that people understand the meanings, grasp the contents, and recognize that the revelation exceeds human capacity; reason apprehends speech’s meaning.
rows.anchor: لعلكم تعقلون أي : لكي تفهموا معانيه وتحيطوا بما فيه وتطلعوا على أنه خارج عن طوق البشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling understanding the divine purpose is figurative; Sunni theology does not say God’s acts are caused by ulterior purposes.
rows.anchor: فإن أفعال الله تعالى لا تعلل بالأغراض عند أهل السنة

rows.speaker: بحر العلوم
rows.claim: Here “perhaps” means divine intent: Arabs receive a revelation in their language and cannot claim they were not addressed; this is contrasted with an untranslated Qur’an.
rows.anchor: وقال في بحر العلوم : لعل مستعار لمعنى الإرادة لتلاحظ العرب معناه

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The letters of alif-lam-ra signify God, Gabriel, and the Messenger, conveying signs from the Beloved to the lover; Arabic clothes the revelation in the audience’s language.
rows.anchor: وفي "التأويلات النجمية" : {الر يشير بألف إلى الله وباللام إلى جبريل

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: Divine speech in its reality is beyond letters, sounds, and languages, but people need linguistic forms to understand its meanings.
rows.anchor: حقيقة كلام الله تعالى منزهة في كلاميته عن كسوة الحروف والأصوات واللغات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Expressions such as God’s saying “We revealed” and “He found you astray” are relative to God and conventional Arabic usage, not indications of deficiency; expression here requires proper reverence.
rows.anchor: مثل هذا التعبير إنما هو بالنسبة إلى الله تعالى وقد تعارفه العرب من غير أن يخطر ببالهم نقص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yusuf is a Hebrew proper name, so it does not decline for foreignness and definiteness; Abraham spoke Hebrew, while Adam spoke Syriac.
rows.anchor: يوسف وهو اسم عبري ولذا لم ينصرف للعجمة والتعريف

rows.speaker: السيوطي
rows.claim: Syriac derives from Saryana, the island region where Noah and his people lived before the Flood; its people spoke Syriac except the Arab Jurhum.
rows.anchor: قال السيوطي السرياني منسوب إلى سريانة وهي أرض الجزيرة التي كان نوح وقومه قبل الغرق فيها

rows.speaker: أنوار المشارق
rows.claim: A linguistic coincidence joins asaf, “grief,” and asif, “servant,” in Yusuf’s grieving father and his son’s name.
rows.anchor: قال في أنوار المشارق : من اللطائف الاتفاقية أن الأسف في اللغة الحزن والأسيف العبد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An etymological tale says Jacob and Esau were twins who fought in the womb; Jacob emerged holding Esau’s heel, while Esau’s name reflects his going out first.
rows.anchor: قال بعض من مال إلى الاشتقاق في هذه الأسماء : إنما سمى يعقوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The tale further says Isaac asked Esau for game and promised a prophetic blessing, but Rebekah sent Jacob in Esau’s clothes with prepared meat to receive it first.
rows.anchor: وكان لكل نبي دعوة مستجابة ، وأخر رسولنا دعاءه للشفاعة العظمى يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dream foreshadows a greater divine choosing, including prophethood; every image seen in the imaginal realm must have a realized counterpart, even though the whole world is a kind of dream.
rows.anchor: فالكاف في محل النصب على أنه صفة مصدر محذوف يجتبيك ربك يختارك ويصطفيك لما هو أعظم منها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects the objection that teaching dream interpretation cannot be included with election in the comparison: it is a substantial gift fitting the context of divine favor.
rows.anchor: يقول الفقير : هذا هو منهما نعمة جسيمة من الله تعالى كما يدل عليه مقام الامتنان فلا سماجة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Interpretation of reports” means interpreting dreams: true dreams are angelic messages, while false ones arise from the self or Satan; interpretation returns the dream to its actual referent.
rows.anchor: والمراد بتأويل الأحاديث تعبير الرؤى جمع الرؤيا ؛ إذ هي إما أحاديث الملك إن كانت صادقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The term ta’wil fits because the interpreter returns the dream to the reality described; hadith can mean new speech and, in common usage, speech generally.
rows.anchor: وتسميتها تأويلا لأنه يؤول أمرها إليه أي يرجع إلى ما يذكره المعبر من حقيقتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Completing Yusuf’s blessing may mean adding kingship to the prophethood implied by election; teaching is placed between them to follow the real-world sequence.
rows.anchor: بأن يضم إلى النبوة المستفادة من الاجتباء الملك ويجعله تتمة لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The blessing on Yusuf is completed as it was for Abraham and Isaac: Abraham became God’s intimate and was saved from fire and sacrificing his son; Isaac’s line produced Jacob and the tribes.
rows.anchor: أما إتمامها على إبراهيم فباتخاذه خليلا وبانجائه من النار ومن ذبح الولد ، وأما على إسحاق

rows.speaker: الكواشي
rows.claim: Calling Abraham and Isaac Yusuf’s fathers reflects their original status as forefathers; a person may be called another’s son across several intervening generations.
rows.anchor: قال في الكواشي الجد أب في الأصالة يقال فلان ابن فلان وبينهما عدة آباء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The comparison does not require the blessing to occur in precisely the same form for Yusuf and for the two forefathers.
rows.anchor: ولا يجب في تحقيق التشبيه كون ذلك في جانب المشبه به مثل ما وقع في جانب المشبه في كل وجه

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: In the inward reading, the heart of Yusuf receives the completed blessing through divine manifestation; the believer’s heart is God’s true throne, unlike heaven and earth.
rows.anchor: والإشارة أن إتمام النعمة على يوسف القلب بأن يتجلى له ويستوى عليه إذ هو عرش حقيقي للرب تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The heart’s disclosure reflects its lights onto the spirit’s offspring, including the senses and faculties, which are the “household of Jacob” in the allegory.
rows.anchor: تنعكس أنوار التجلي من مرآة القلب على جميع المتولدات من الروح كالحواس والقوى وغيرهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is knowing and wise because He selects the worthy and gives blessings to those who deserve them; the order of these names shifts with the relation between knowledge and wisdom in the unseen and manifest realms.
rows.anchor: أما الأول فباعتبار حضرة العلم لأن العلم في تعلقه في الأعيان والحقائق العلمية تابع للحكمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the realm of concrete forms, wisdom follows knowledge and orders each thing according to its preparedness; this account is attributed to the author’s spiritual guide.
rows.anchor: كذا في بعض تحريرات شيخنا الأجل ومرشدنا الأكمل قدس الله نفسه الزاكية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The story is a sign of God’s power and wisdom: the brothers sought to abase Yusuf, but God raised him to prophethood and kingship and made them submit, turning their envy back on them.
rows.anchor: أي بالله قد كان في قصة يوسف وحكاية إخوته الأحد عشر.

rows.speaker: التفسير الفارسي
rows.claim: A Persian account says the brothers’ wives heard of Yusuf’s dream and Jacob’s warning to conceal it, then told the brothers, stirring their envy.
rows.anchor: وفي التفسير الفارسي (آورده اندكه ون يوسف خواب مذكوررا بادر تقرير كرد

rows.speaker: يهودا وروبيل وشمعون
rows.claim: Judah, Reuben, and Simeon objected that their brothers would bow to Yusuf and their parents would bow as well, so they plotted to remove him.
rows.anchor: وقال يهودا وروبيل وشمعون : ما رضي أن يسجد له إخوته حتى يسجد له أبواه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The emphatic lām makes the brothers’ claim that Yusuf is especially loved certain in their view; “his brother” means full brother Benjamin, left unnamed to emphasize their shared parents.
rows.anchor: فلام الابتداء لتحقيق مضمون الجملة وتأكيده أي إن زيادة محبته لهما أمر محقق ثابت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Full brother” ordinarily means sharing both parents, though the term may also be explained through sharing the father or mother.
rows.anchor: والشقيق الأخ من الأب والأم

rows.speaker: بعض العارفين
rows.claim: Some gnostics say Jacob favored Yusuf because the dream disclosed his complete potential: he would inherit his father and grandfather and gather his brothers’ capacities.
rows.anchor: قال بعض العارفين : مال يعقوب إلى يوسف لظهور كمال استعداده الكلي في رؤياه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation is that God meant to test Jacob through his love for Yusuf, intensifying the trial by making him absent from his father.
rows.anchor: وقيل لأن الله تعالى أراد ابتلاءه محبته إليه في قلبه ثم غيبه عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Divine love does not accept a rival in its kingdom: no one should become a veil alongside God, and a child’s plot can wound a parent more than other calamities.
rows.anchor: إذ سلطان المحبة لا يقبل الشركة في ملكه ، والجمال والكمال في الحقيقةتعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob’s sons call themselves a strong group worthy of their father’s affection; the author defines the band as ten or more men, whose solidarity strengthens affairs.
rows.anchor: أي : والحال أنا جماعة قادرون على الحل والعقد أحقاء بالمحبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers infer injustice from the apparent smallness of the two boys, but fail to understand Yusuf’s real worth.
rows.anchor: نظروا إلى صورة يوسف ولم يحيطوا علما بمعناه فقالوا ما قالوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rumi’s poem uses an old man and a younger person to show that appearance and precedence do not prove greater maturity or better character.
rows.anchor: خوى زشت تو نكر ديده است وشت

rows.speaker: الكواشي
rows.claim: There is no pause from “for those who ask” through “righteous,” since the brothers’ quoted sentence continues; a breath break requires reconnecting the clauses.
rows.anchor: قال في الكواشي : لا وقف من السائلين إلى صالحين لأن الكلام جملة محكية عنهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The imperative “kill” is read with kasra or damma; kasra is common, while damma follows the rounded vowel of the verb’s second radical.
rows.anchor: {اقتلوا يوسف} بكسر وضم والمشهور الكسر ، وجه الضم التبعية لعين الفعل وهي مضمومة

rows.speaker: الإمام
rows.claim: Answering the objection that envy and attempted murder contradict prophetic impeccability, the Imam says infallibility is required once prophethood begins, not before.
rows.anchor: قلت : المعتبر عصمة الأنبياء في وقت حصول النبوة فأما ما قبلها فذلك غير واجب كذا أجاب الامام

rows.speaker: شرح العقائد
rows.claim: Another theological statement says prophets are protected from unbelief before and after revelation by consensus, and from deliberately committing major sins.
rows.anchor: وفي شرح العقائد : الأنبياء معصومون من الكفر قبل الوحي وبعده بالإجماع وكذا من تعمد الكبائر

rows.speaker: تيسير
rows.claim: A report says Satan appeared to the brothers and warned that Yusuf might enslave them, prompting their proposal to kill him.
rows.anchor: درتيسير آورده كه ون شيطان ابن كلمات از ايشان استماع كرد بصورت يرى رشان ظاهر شد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unspecified land means an unknown, distant place where Yusuf would die or be eaten by beasts; grammatically it is an indefinite adverbial place, not any land whatsoever.
rows.anchor: أرضا منكورة مجهولة بعيدة من العمران ليهلك فيها أو يأكله السباع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The inward lesson equates banishment with killing: rulers who exile scholars and sheikhs sever them from children and followers and thus destroy them socially.
rows.anchor: وفيه إشارة إلى أن التغريب يساوي القتل كما في قوله تعالى : ولولا أن كتب الله عليهم الجلاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Your father’s face” pictures his turning wholly toward them; “after him” means after Yusuf’s case is finished, when they claim they will become righteous.
rows.anchor: أي : يخلص لكم وجه أبيكم فيقبل عليكم بكليته ولا يلتفت عنكم إلى غيركم

rows.speaker: أبو الليث
rows.claim: The brothers did not mean forbidden play; they meant harmless joking, which Abu Layth says is permissible. Ali likewise allows humor that eases a person’s sternness.
rows.anchor: قال أبو الليث : لم يريدوا به اللعب الذي هو منهى عنه ، وإنما أرادوا به المطايبة في المزاح في غير مأثم

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Ali says humor is acceptable when it helps a person leave behind a forbidding, stern manner.
rows.anchor: قال أمير المؤمنين علي رضي الله عنه : لا بأس بفكاهة يخرج بها الإنسان من حد العبوس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A comic incident has Ali tell an accuser to stand in the sun and strike the accused man’s shadow, a joke about the allegation.
rows.anchor: روى أنه أتى رجل برجل إلى علي فقال إن هذا زعم أنه احتلم على أمي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob’s sadness comes from separation from Yusuf and his limited patience in enduring it.
rows.anchor: وذلك لشدة وفارقته علي وقلة صبري عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the initiating lām usually marks a present verb, the going is future; the author resolves this by taking the present sense as Jacob’s present intention or anticipation.
rows.anchor: إن التقدير قصد أن تذهبوا به والقصد حال أو تصور ذهابكم وتوقعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob fears a wolf because the land was known for wolves; sadness is pain at losing what one loves, while fear is disturbance at expected harm.
rows.anchor: واللام للعهد الذهني ، والحزن ألم القلب بفوت المحبوب ، والخوف انزعاج النفس لنزول المكروه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob had dreamed that eleven wolves attacked Yusuf on a plain and he disappeared among them, explaining the specific warning about a wolf.
rows.anchor: وروى أنه رأى في المنام كأنه على رأس جبل ويوسف في صحراء فهجم عليه أحد عشر ذئبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though Jacob fears the danger, he gives Yusuf to his brothers because destiny can blind a person’s sight; Persian verse illustrates that one sees danger yet cannot escape fate.
rows.anchor: ومع ذلك فقد دفعه إلى إخوته لأنه إذا جاء القضاء عمي البصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers insist that, as a powerful band, they could protect Yusuf and would be the losers if a wolf nevertheless ate him.
rows.anchor: قالوا والله لئن أكله الذئب ونحن عصبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “When they took him” connects to an omitted permission and sending by Jacob; the omitted response is that they inflicted the abuse later described.
rows.anchor: به متصل بمحذوف ، أي : فأذن له وأرسله معهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob yielded after Yusuf’s brothers persisted in asking to take him to the open country, swore emphatically, and Yusuf himself wanted an outing.
rows.anchor: أن يعقوب عليه السلام لما رأى إلحاح أخوة يوسف في خروجه معهم إلى الصحراء ومبالغتهم بالعهد واليمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The narrative says Gabriel had brought Abraham the basin used when the ram was sacrificed; Yusuf was washed, groomed, oiled, and kohl-lined before departure.
rows.anchor: فأمر أن يغسل بدن يوسف في طست كان أتى به جبريل إلى إبراهيم حين مجيء الفداء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A transmitted story traces Yusuf’s shirt from Gabriel’s gift to Abraham in the fire, through Isaac and Jacob, who hid it in an amulet around Yusuf’s neck.
rows.anchor: ويروى أن إبراهيم عليه السلام حين ألقي في النار وجرد عن ثيابه أتاه جبريل بقميص من حرير الجنة

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Kashifi describes Jacob fastening the amulet, accompanying his sons to the farewell tree, embracing Yusuf and weeping; Yusuf asks his father not to forget him.
rows.anchor: وقال الكاشفي (ون تعويذي بربازويش بست وبمشايعه فر زندان تاشجرة الوداع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers carried Yusuf on their shoulders as an honor and sign of joy while Jacob watched and wept from longing.
rows.anchor: وهم جعلوا يحملونه على عواتقهم إكراماله وسرورا به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A caravan traveling from Midian to Egypt stopped near Yusuf’s well three days after he was thrown in; Kashifi instead says rescue came on the fourth day.
rows.anchor: {وجآءت سيارة} جماعة يسيرون من جهة مدين إلى مصر

rows.speaker: السمرقندي
rows.claim: Samarqandi says the well stood in a remote desert used only by shepherds and the travelers had lost their way.
rows.anchor: قال السمرقندي في بحر العلوم : كان الجب في قفرة بعيدة من العمران لم يكن إلا للرعاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The remote-well account conflicts with the verse’s implication that a passing caravan could readily find the well on a safe, traveled route.
rows.anchor: فهذا يخالف قوله تعالى : يلتقطه بعض السيارة فإنه يقتضي كون الجب في الأمن والجادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The caravan sent its water drawer, Malik ibn D’ar al-Khuza‘i, to draw water; Yusuf was inspired to hold onto the rope.
rows.anchor: وكان ذلك مالك بن دعر الخزاعي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The well’s walls wept at Yusuf’s absence because inanimate things possess a real life, remembrance, and fellowship with people of God.
rows.anchor: وذلك لأن للجمادات حياة حقانية لا يعرفها إلا العلماء بالله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author calls the report sound that the tree trunk the Prophet leaned on groaned when he left it after a pulpit was made.
rows.anchor: وقد صح أن الجزع الذي كان يعتمد عليه رسول الله حين الموعظة للناس أن أنين بني آدم لما فارقه رسول الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rumi’s poem presents the groaning trunk as an intelligent being crying from separation from the Messenger.
rows.anchor: استن حنانه از هجر رسول ناله مى زد همو أرباب عقول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yusuf emerged as an exceptionally beautiful boy; Malik exclaims “good news” as if summoning glad tidings to come enjoy this rare find.
rows.anchor: فلما خرج يوسف إذا هو بغلام أحسن ما يكون وقد كان أعطى شطر الحسن

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Kashifi offers another reading: “my good news” is a companion whom Malik calls to help bring Yusuf out of the well.
rows.anchor: وقيل : هو اسم صاحب له ناداه ليعينه على إخراجه ، كما قال الكاشفي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The purchaser was Qitfir, Aziz over Egypt’s treasuries and the king’s troops; Aziz is a title for the ruler of a kingdom.
rows.anchor: وهو العزيز الذي كان على خزائن مصر وصاحب جنود الملك واسمه قطفير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The king at the time was Rayyan ibn al-Walid; after believing in Yusuf he died during Yusuf’s life, and Qabus ibn Mus‘ab succeeded him but refused Yusuf’s invitation to Islam.
rows.anchor: وكان الملك يومئذ الريان بن الوليد من العماليق مات في حياة يوسف بعد أن آمن به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Pharaoh of Moses descended from Yusuf’s Pharaoh, so addressing later Egyptians about Yusuf in 40:34 is an address to descendants about their ancestors.
rows.anchor: وكان فرعون موسى من أولاد فرعون يوسف فقوله تعالى : ولقد جاءكم يوسف من قبل بالبينات

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Kashifi recounts that Egyptian agents saw Yusuf’s beauty, became captivated, and reported him to the Aziz, who sought to buy him.
rows.anchor: قال الكاشفي : (ون خبر كاروان مدين بمصر آمد وكماشتكان عزيز بسرراه كاروان آمده يوسف را ديدند

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Inwardly, the self’s faculties cannot value the heart and trade it for fleeting pleasures, while the heart is prepared for lasting and divine joys; its spiritual overflow benefits the senses and soul.
rows.anchor: والحواس والقوى لا تعرف قدر القلب وتبيعه بأدنى حظ نفس فان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Giving whatever one can in pursuit of the beloved is a sign of love; each person benefits according to the worth of what they offer.
rows.anchor: وفيه إشارة إلى أنه ينبغي لكل أحد بذل ما في ملكه مما قدر عليه في طريق المطلوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account dates Yusuf’s arrival at seventeen, prison for thirteen years, appointment as minister at thirty, wisdom at thirty-three, and death at 120; it says he first made paper.
rows.anchor: وكان سن يوسف إذ ذاك سبع عشرة سنة ، وأقام في منزل العزيز مع ما مر عليه من مدة لبثه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām in “for his wife” attaches to “he said,” not “he bought”; the wife is named Ra‘il with variant parentage and the familiar title Zulaikha.
rows.anchor: {لامرأته} اللام متعلقة بقال لا باشترى ، أي قال لامرأته راعيل بنت رعاييل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Make his stay gracious” means provide a pleasant residence and attend to his food and needs, using the place as a respectful metonym for the person.
rows.anchor: أكرمي مثويه اجعلي محل إقامته كريما حسنا مرضيا والمعنى أحسني تعهده في المطعم والمشرب وغيرهما

rows.speaker: الإمام الغزالي
rows.claim: Ghazali explains that calling a noble person “the presence,” “the court,” or “the assembly” honors him through what is associated with him.
rows.anchor: قال الإمام الغزالي رحمه الله : يكنى عن الشريف بالجناب والحضرة والمجلس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Aziz hopes Yusuf may help with their needs; adoption is also possible because the wife had no child and he perceived Yusuf’s good judgment.
rows.anchor: أو نتخذه ولدا أي نتبناه ونقيمه مقام الولد ، وإنه لم يكن لها ولد وقد تفرس فيه الرشد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Three people are said to have unusual foresight: Egypt’s Aziz, Shu‘ayb’s daughter who recommended hiring Moses, and Abu Bakr in choosing Umar.
rows.anchor: ولذلك قيل افرس الناس ثلاثة : عزيز مصر وابنة شعيب التي قالت : يا أبت استأجره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The establishment in the land means Egypt; the demonstrative points to the later act of establishing, with the comparison particle serving to exalt this remarkable placement.
rows.anchor: {وكذالك مكنا ليوسف فى الأرض} أي : جعلنا له فيها مكانا والمراد أرض مصر وهي أربعون فرسخا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yusuf was displayed at auction for three days as the buyers bid against one another; the price grew beyond what anyone could afford.
rows.anchor: وعرض في بيع من يزيد ثلاثة أيام فزاد الناس بعضهم على بعض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yusuf was purchased for his weight in musk, pearls, gold, silver, and silk; an old woman brought yarn hoping to buy him, as Jami’s poem recalls.
rows.anchor: فاشتراه عزيز مصر بوزنه مرة مسكا ومرة لؤلؤا ومرة ذهبا ومرة فضة ومرة حريرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The story says Yusuf’s weight was four hundred ratls and an old woman offered some spun yarn to purchase him.
rows.anchor: وكان وزنه أربعمائة رطل وحكى أن عجوزا أحضرت شيئا من الغزل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Teaching dream interpretation, especially the king’s and the two prisoners’ dreams, leads Yusuf to supreme authority.
rows.anchor: ولنعلمه من تأويل الأحاديث أي : نوفقه لتعبير بعض المنامات التي عمدتها رؤيا الملك وصاحبي السجن

rows.speaker: أبو الليث
rows.claim: Abu Layth says dream interpretation is included along with other kinds of knowledge.
rows.anchor: وفي "تفسير أبي الليث" : من تأويل الأحاديث ، يعني : تعبير الرؤيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God completely governs His own affair and Yusuf’s: nothing can resist what He wills, though most people mistakenly assume they control events.
rows.anchor: الهاء راجعة إلى الله أي على أمر نفسه لا يرده شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An attributed divine saying tells Adam’s children that surrender to God’s will brings what they want, while resisting it exhausts them without changing the outcome.
rows.anchor: وجاء في بعض الآثار أن الله تعالى يقول : ابن آدم تريد وأريد ولا يكون إلا ما أريد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Proper adab with God means surrendering to what He discloses in the present moment rather than wanting to bring about another state.
rows.anchor: فالأدب مع الله تعالى أن يستسلم العبد لما أظهره الله تعالى في الوقت

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: In the inward allegory, Yusuf leaves the well of nature for Egypt as the realm of sacred law; the Aziz is a guide on the path who leads toward reality.
rows.anchor: وفي التأويلات النجمية لما أخرجوه من جب الطبيعة ذهبوا به إلى مصر الشريعة

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The Aziz’s wife is the lower world; she should serve the body’s necessary needs, while Yusuf’s prophetic alchemy can transform law into reality and worldly life into the afterlife.
rows.anchor: وهي الدنيا اكرمي مثواه أخدمي له في منزل الجسد بقدر حاجته الماسة

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: Alternatively, adopting Yusuf means nourishing the heart with the milk of law and the spiritual path until it is weaned from the low world.
rows.anchor: أو نتخذه ولدا نربيه بلبان ثديي الشريعة والطريقة والفطام عن الدنيا الدنية

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The heart must be rooted in human embodiment for the fruits of religious knowledge and divine witnessing to appear, just as a tree needs roots in the earth.
rows.anchor: فكما أن الثمرة على الشجرة إنما تظهر إذا كان أصل الشجرة راسخا في الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The remarkable placement Yusuf received is recompense for his good action; linking reward to the good-doers signals that virtue causes it.
rows.anchor: وفي تعليق الجزاء المذكور بالمحسنين إشعار بعلية الإحسان له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God gave Yusuf judgment and knowledge because he acted well and remained God-fearing in his early years.
rows.anchor: إنما آتاه الحكم والعلم لكونه محسنا في أعماله متقيا في عنفوان أمره

rows.speaker: بعض الأكابر
rows.claim: Some spiritual authorities define the good-doers as those who excel in seeking, intention, striving, and discipline; God loves them and grants happiness in both worlds.
rows.anchor: قال بعض الأكابر : نجزي المحسنين الذين يحسنون لأنفسهم في الطلب والإرادة والاجتهاد والرياضة

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A hadith says that when God loves a servant He tells Gabriel, then the angels and people of earth come to love that person.
rows.anchor: في الحديث : "إذا أحب الله العبد نادى جبريل إن الله يحب فلانا

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: When the heart reaches maturity and readiness for divine effusion, God bestows judgment, wisdom, and knowledge from His presence.
rows.anchor: وفي "التأويلات النجمية" : {ولما بلغ أشده}

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The principal limbs and organs receive the best reward when their conduct and character follow the law and the spiritual path, culminating in the station of reality.
rows.anchor: وكرمنا كذلك نجزي المحسنين الأعضاء الرئيسية والجوارح إذا أحسنوا الأعمال والأخلاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reward may follow completion of all work or accrue after each completed act; Yusuf received dream interpretation in prison and full knowledge after his trial ended.
rows.anchor: فعلم تعبير رؤيا الملك وصاحبي السجن أوتى يوسف في السجن وتمامه مع انضمام العلوم الكلية بعد انتهاء الابتلاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shirt torn from behind reveals Yusuf’s truthfulness and innocence, as Jami’s poem dramatizes the Aziz checking the garment.
rows.anchor: وعلم براءة يوسف وصدقه كما قال الجامي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Aziz says the incident is part of women’s plotting, and addresses women generally to show that the trait is deeply rooted in them.
rows.anchor: قال إنه أي الأمر الذي وقع فيه التشاجر من كيدكن من جنس حيلتكن ومكركن أيتها النساء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Women’s plotting is called great because it clings to the heart and affects the psyche more than men’s, or because women direct men while Satan only whispers secretly.
rows.anchor: فإنه ألصق وأعلق بالقلب وأشد تأثيرا في النفس

rows.speaker: بعض العلماء
rows.claim: An unnamed scholar says he fears women more than Satan, since the Qur’an calls Satan’s plotting weak but women’s plotting great.
rows.anchor: وعن بعض العلماء أنا أخاف من النساء ما لا أخاف من الشيطان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Aziz tells Yusuf to keep silent about the matter to prevent public scandal, and tells Zulaikha to seek forgiveness for the deliberate sin she committed.
rows.anchor: يوسف أي قال العزيز يا يوسف اعرض عن هذا الأمر وعن التحديد به واكتمه حتى لا يشيع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The masculine plural in “you were among the sinners” follows the convention of giving the masculine form precedence; a hadith says all children of Adam err and the best errers repent.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث : كل ابن آدم خطاء وخير الخطائين التوابون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Aziz was patient and satisfied with this rebuke; one report says he swore not to visit her for forty days and removed Yusuf to serve him.
rows.anchor: وقيل كان قليل الغيرة وروى أنه حلف أن لا يدخل عليها إلى أربعين يوما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The women of the city are identified as the wives of the baker, cupbearer, animal keeper, prison keeper, and chamberlain.
rows.anchor: وكن خمسا امرأة الخباز ، وامرأة الساقي وامرأة صاحب الدواب ، وامرأة صاحب السجن

rows.speaker: الرضي
rows.claim: Al-Radi analyzes niswah as a plural because it follows the pattern of ghulmah, rather than as a collective noun with no singular.
rows.anchor: وقال الرضى : النسوة جمع لأنها على وزن فعلة فيقدر لها مفرد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The women’s gossip spread the story despite the Aziz’s attempt to contain it; love is accompanied by public reproach, which can intensify love and its fame.
rows.anchor: وبعض از خواتين مصر زبان ملامت برزليخا درازكرد

rows.speaker: الحافظ
rows.claim: Hafez says Yusuf’s increasing beauty made him understand how love could draw Zulaikha beyond the bounds of chastity.
rows.anchor: قال الحافظ : من أزان حسن روزافزون كه يوسف داشت دانستم

rows.speaker: الجامي
rows.claim: Jami says love cannot settle in safety: blame renews its sorrow and makes its voice louder.
rows.anchor: وقال الجامي : نسازد عشق راكنج سلامت خوشا رسوايي وكويى ملامت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “In the city” can be an adverb modifying “said” or a description of the women; Kashifi places their conversation at Ain al-Shams in Egypt.
rows.anchor: في المدينة ظرف لقال ، أي أشعن الأمر في مصر أو صفة للنسوة

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Kashifi says the women were sitting together in the city of Egypt when they spoke about the matter.
rows.anchor: وقال الكاشفي : (با يكديكر نشسته كفتند در شهر مصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Aziz” is an Arabic title for a king but here means Qitfir, minister to Rayyan; custom avoids naming rulers and their close household women.
rows.anchor: والمراد به قطفير وزير الريان وبامرأته زليخا ولم يصرحن باسمها

rows.speaker: سعدي المفتي
rows.claim: Sa‘di says describing her as the Aziz’s wife heightens the scandal because people are especially interested in news about nobles.
rows.anchor: وقال سعدي المفتي : صرحن بإضافتها إلى العزيز مبالغة للتشنيع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “She seeks her young servant” means she solicits intercourse, schemes, and tries to entice him; “young man” can designate a slave even if he is old.
rows.anchor: أي : تطالب غلامها بمواقعته لها وتحتال في ذلك وتخادعه عن نفسه

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A hadith discourages owners from saying “my male or female slave,” recommending “my boy,” “my girl,” or “my young servant” because all belong to God.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث : لا يقولن أحدكم عبدي وأمتي كلكم عبيد الله

rows.speaker: ابن الملك
rows.claim: Ibn al-Malik says the wording is disliked when used to exalt the owner or demean the enslaved person; another qualification says the Qur’an itself uses servant language.
rows.anchor: قال ابن الملك : إنما كره النبي عليه السلام أن يقول السيد عبدي لأن فيه تعظيما لنفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Her love pierced the covering of the heart and reached the core; grammatically, “with love” is a specification transferred from the subject.
rows.anchor: وهو بيان لاختلال أحوالها القلبية كأحوالها القالبية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yusuf promises to identify each arriving meal’s kind, quantity, color, taste, and other qualities before it reaches the prisoners.
rows.anchor: بأن بينت لكما ماهيته من أي جنس هو ومقداره وكيفيته من اللون والطعم وسائر أحواله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception is an all-inclusive exception of circumstances: no food arrives under any condition except that Yusuf has already told its interpretation.
rows.anchor: ألا نبأتكما بتأويله استثناء مفرغ من أعم الأحوال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the meal’s explanation “interpretation” is metaphorical: explaining an unspecified meal resembles interpreting an unspecified dream.
rows.anchor: وإطلاق التأويل عليه بطريق الاستعارة فإن ذلك بالنسبة إلى مطلق الطعام المبهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jesus likewise announced what people ate and stored in their homes, a parallel for knowledge of unseen matters.
rows.anchor: كما قال : {وأنبئكم بما تأكلون وما تدخرون فى بيوتكم}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rumi’s poem contrasts bodily physicians who infer illness from pulse and appearance with perfected spiritual knowers who perceive a person’s inward condition from afar and even before birth.
rows.anchor: كاملان ازدور نامت بشنوند تا بقعر تارو بودت درروند

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yusuf names his prophetic ancestors so the prisoners recognize his noble lineage, trust him, and listen; a learned person may identify his rank when necessary so others can benefit.
rows.anchor: عرف شرف نسبه وأنه من أهل بيت النبوة لتتقوى رغبتهما في الاستماع منه والوثوق عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A hadith says God will ask a person about the benefit of his knowledge just as He asks about his wealth; clearing away false belief precedes acquiring true belief.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث : إن الله يسأل الرجل عن فضل علمه كما يسأله عن فضل ماله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the inward reading, Abraham signifies the secret, Isaac hiddenness, and Jacob the spirit; the prophetic way is tawhid and knowledge.
rows.anchor: والإشارة أن ملة إبراهيم السر وإسحاق الخفاء ويعقوب الروح التوحيد والمعرفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is unfit for prophets, given their strong souls and abundant knowledge, to associate anything with God; monotheism is a grace conveyed through revelation to all people by their guidance.
rows.anchor: ما صح وما استقام فضلا عن الوقوع لنا معاشر الأنبياء لقوة نفوسنا ووفور علومنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People should be grateful to prophets and perfected saints as intermediaries of guidance; many recipients instead turn away and fail to thank them.
rows.anchor: ولما كان الأنبياء وكمل الأولياء وسائط بين الله وخلقه لزم شكرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Addressing the prisoners as companions in the difficult place of imprisonment softens the argument, since shared hardship creates affection and sincere counsel.
rows.anchor: لما ذكر ما هو عليه من الدين القويم تلطف في حسن الاستدلال على فساد ما عليه قوم الفتيين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Many scattered lords” means separate idols of different sizes and materials, from gold and silver to iron, wood, and stone.
rows.anchor: ءارباب متفرقون الاستفهام إنكاري (آيا خدايان راكنده كه شما داريد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rhetorical question contrasts scattered lords with God, the true, singular deity who overcomes all rivals; worldly life, appetite, and Satan only seem good to those they mislead.
rows.anchor: خير لكما أم الله المعبود بالحق الواحد المنفرد بالألوهية القهار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “What you worship” addresses the two prisoners and everyone following their religion; whatever is besides God consists only of names without real referents.
rows.anchor: ما تعبدون الخطاب لهما ولمن على دينهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The invented names have no external reality and no revealed warrant; only God has the right to decide worship because He exists necessarily, creates all, and owns all.
rows.anchor: إلا أسماء مجردة لا مطابق لها في الخارج لأن ما ليس فيه مصداق إطلاق الاسم عليه لا وجود له أصلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s command through the prophets is to worship Him alone; this exclusive worship is the upright religion, Islam, whose principles remain one although branches vary with peoples’ capacities.
rows.anchor: ذلك تخصيصه تعالى بالعبادة الدين القيم أي الثابت أو المستقيم وهو دين الإسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most people persist in ignorance because they do not know the truth about God’s exclusive right to worship.
rows.anchor: {ولاكن أكثر الناس لا يعلمون} فيخبطون في جهالتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Everything besides God is a passing shadow; the discerning person follows the Creator of the shadow by obeying His commands and avoiding open and hidden associationism.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن ما سوى الله تعالى ظل زائل ، والعاقل لا يتبع الظل بل يتبع من خلق الظل

rows.speaker: بعض الفضلاء
rows.claim: A spiritual authority says faith and obedience benefit only when desired for their own sake, not for reward or fear of punishment.
rows.anchor: قال بعض الفضلاء : الرغبة في الإيمان والطاعة لا تنفع إلا إذا كانت تلك الرغبة رغبة فيه

rows.speaker: امرأة
rows.claim: In an anecdote, a woman says giving money is ordinary generosity, and even exerting oneself in worship is not selfless if one expects reward in return.
rows.anchor: وحكى أن أمرة قالت لجماعة ما السخاء عندكم؟ قالوا : بذل المال قالت هو سخاء أهل الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: True worship seeks neither Paradise nor fear of Hell nor reward; it requires spiritual stripping and unity, through which a person draws near to God and acts with divinely granted insight.
rows.anchor: العملتعالى لا للجنة ولا للنار ولا للثواب وخوف العقاب

rows.speaker: أبو بكر الكتاني
rows.claim: Al-Kattani tells of a watchful youth in Sana’a who preferred hearing “the Provider” directly to listening to Abd al-Razzaq and correctly identified al-Khidr.
rows.anchor: قال أبو بكر الكتاني قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The story illustrates saints who exchange fleeting life for lasting life, efface themselves for true existence, and perceive the forms and meanings of creation.
rows.anchor: فلله عباد قد بدلوا الحياة الفانية بالحياة الباقية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The courtiers call the king’s dream muddled falsehoods from self-talk or Satanic whispering; a hadith distinguishes dreams from God, distressing dreams from Satan, and one’s own thoughts.
rows.anchor: قالوا هي : اضغاث أحلام تخاليطها أي أباطيلها وأكاذيبها من حديث نفس أو وسوسة شيطان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word adghath is the plural of dighth, a mixed handful of fresh and dry grass; the phrase describes dreams whose elements are too confused for sound interpretation.
rows.anchor: قال في القاموس الغضث بالكسر قبضة حشيش مختلطة الرطب باليابس

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A prophetic report contrasts a true dream from God with a false dream from Satan.
rows.anchor: لقوله عليه السلام الرؤيا من الله والحلم من الشيطان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Using the plural “muddled dreams” despite one vision intensifies the judgment that it is false, or reflects its many mixed elements such as the seven cows and ears of grain.
rows.anchor: وجمعوا الضغث مع أن الرؤيا واحدة مبالغة في وصفها بالبطلان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “We are not knowledgeable in dream interpretation” may mean the dream has no interpretation because it is false, or that the speakers lack expertise to interpret a potentially meaningful dream.
rows.anchor: وما نحن بتأويل الأحلام أي المنامات الباطلة التي لا أصل لها بعالمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author also entertains that they admit their limited expertise; the king’s conditional “if you interpret dreams” implies that he does not regard them as established experts.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون ذلك اعترافا منهم بقصور علمهم وأنهم ليسوا بنحارير في تأويل الأحلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God may have blocked their answer so Yusuf could be released and his excellence made visible.
rows.anchor: وعلى تقدير تبحرهم عمى الله عليهم ، وأعجزهم عن الجواب ليصير ذلك سببا لخلاص يوسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yusuf calls himself a careful guardian and knowledgeable because he protects himself from harm and understands how to use his position for benefit rather than harm.
rows.anchor: ولهذا قال يوسف إني حفيظ عليم أي : حافظ نفسي فيها عما يضرها عليم بنفعها وضرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Thus” compares Yusuf’s placement with the remarkable recompense just described; God rescued him from prison and made him the king’s close associate.
rows.anchor: {وكذالك} الكاف منصوبة بالتمكين وذلك إشارة إلى ما أنعم الله به عليه من إنجائه من غم الحبس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Establishing Yusuf in the land means giving him a place in Egypt, described as forty farsakhs by forty; another lexicon defines empowerment as granting ability.
rows.anchor: أي : جعلنا له مكانا في الأرض أي أرض مصر وكانت أربعين فرسخا في أربعين كما في الإرشاد

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abu Ali parses Yusuf’s settling wherever he wishes as a circumstantial phrase, expressing his complete authority and freedom of movement throughout the land.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو علي : يجوز أن يكون على حد ردف لكم يتبوأ منها حال من يوسف

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A hadith says that had Yusuf not asked to manage the storehouses, the king would have appointed him immediately, but Yusuf delayed the request for a year.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث : رحم الله أخي يوسف لو لم يقل اجعلني على خزائن الأرض لاستعمله من ساعته

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says that after a year the king invested Yusuf with royal insignia and delegated rule; Yusuf accepted the throne and administrative symbols but said the crown was not his family’s dress.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما لما انصرمت السنة من يوم سأل الإمارة دعاه الملك فتوجه وختمه بخاتمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The later account says Yusuf ruled justly and organized seven years of planting, storing grain in its husks and saving a fifth of the harvest before famine arrived.
rows.anchor: وأمر أهل كل قرية وبلدة بالاشتغال بالزرع وترك غيره فلم يدعوا مكانا إلا زرعوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: During famine Yusuf sold food for increasingly valuable goods, eventually receiving people’s land, children, and persons; he then freed everyone and restored their property.
rows.anchor: وباع من أهل مصر في سني القحط الطعام في السنة الأولى بالدراهم والدنانير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening exhortation urges holding fast to piety, whose outcome is sound, rather than other attachments that break and bring no benefit.
rows.anchor: فعلى العاقل أن يتمسك بعروة التقوى ، فإنها لا انفصام لها ، ولها عاقبة حميدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A Persian account says famine reached Canaan and Syria; Jacob’s sons heard that Egypt’s king helped the hungry and travelers, and Jacob sent ten sons while keeping Benjamin with him.
rows.anchor: (آورده اندكه اثر قحط بكنعان وبلاد شام رسيده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another account says the sons feared Egypt’s tyrannical rulers and Jacob replied that a just king now governed there; he sent them to Yusuf with greetings and confidence he would meet their need.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم : لما أجدبت بلاد الشام وغلت أسعارها جمع يعقوب بنيه وقال لهم يا بني أما ترون ما نحن فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The route from Canaan to Egypt was eight stages; God concealed Yusuf’s location from Jacob and withheld Yusuf’s permission to reveal himself until the appointed time, bringing the brothers there through famine.
rows.anchor: وكانت بين كنعان ومصر ثماني مراحل لكن أبهم الله تعالى ليعقوب عليه السلام مكان يوسف
